findings.page: Run page (04, 09, 13) and every node page (05-12)
findings.problem: The run has no timeline. Events appear only as 'Events for this node' at the very bottom of the node inspector. To reconstruct what happened when, the user has to click each of the 8+ nodes one at a time and scroll to the end of each page. The run page, run list and graph show no time for any step.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:466-487 is the only place events render. RunView.tsx:164-214 shows the node list with status and attempt only. Events sit at ~19,700px of 19,834px on launch_game (06-full; cropped: Launch receipt ~19,400, events ~19,680), ~4,400 of 4,965px on verify_game (07-full), ~3,050 of 3,217px on review (08-full) and ~3,300 of 3,464px on the native review (10-full). On mobile the verify page is 9,024px tall with events last (07-mobile-full). The user's own docs/AI_ROADMAP_REPORT.md:82 and :94-108 contain a hand-built 'Window (UTC)' table and narrative ('verify_controller failed once, passed at 20:18; candidate blocked twice (20:24, 20:27)'), which is exactly what the viewer should show.
findings.user_impact: This is the direct cause of the complaint 'I need to look around to understand what's where, when it happened'. There is no way to read the run's story in one place, including while a live run is being watched.
findings.data_available: GET .../runs/{run}/events already returns every event (sequence, occurred_at, node_id, attempt, status, message) and is already fetched once per run page (RunView.tsx:44-45) and polled. Durations can be enriched from inputs (launch.native_started_at, stop.confirmed_at, questions[].asked_at/answered_at, challenge.decided_at), reviews (reviewers[].launched_at/accepted_at, reviewed_at) and results (checks[].started_at/finished_at). No backend change is needed for a first version.
findings.suggestion: Add a run-level 'Timeline' view, the default Run tab content or a section above the graph. It is a chronological list grouped by node or phase. Each row shows local time, relative time, a node label linking to the node, a status chip, the message and the gap since the previous row. Consecutive 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID' lines collapse into 'controller resumed'. Newest-first order is useful for live runs. Keep 'Events for this node' as a filtered view of the same component, and move it to the top of the node inspector as a compact 'History' strip.

findings.problem: Events with node_id null are never rendered anywhere. They include the controller's own diagnosis and next-step guidance, the operator's repairs, and every controller restart or resume.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:305 filters by event.node_id === node.node_id, and RunView renders no events. Hidden in skeleton-001.events.json: #19 09:21:32 'worker/game failed identically on attempts 1 and 2; not transient, inspect <path> Before review a code fix is a lane repair (RUNBOOK)', #21 09:27:09 'Repair 1 applied: checkpoint forked from 1f1b7f90 (after handoff); attempts worker:game 3', and #10/#15/#18/#22/#26 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID …', which mark every resume. In total 7 of 26 events (41m37s of activity) are hidden. skeleton-fixes-001 #10 is hidden the same way.
findings.user_impact: Why a run stalled and what the operator did (repair, resume) is invisible. The user cannot tell when they resumed the controller or read the 'what to do next' hint the controller logged.
findings.data_available: The same events payload, rows with node_id null and type 'log'.
findings.suggestion: Render them as run-level rows in the timeline, for example 'Controller resumed (PID 3263135)', 'Operator repair 1 applied' and 'Diagnosis: failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 → lane repair (RUNBOOK)'. Highlight diagnosis rows as 'next step'.

findings.page: Run page, node list, graph, every node inspector, checks list
findings.problem: The UI shows no duration anywhere: not per run, not per node, not per attempt, not per check, not per reviewer. formatDuration exists but is used only for configured timeouts. Checks show two absolute timestamps ('09:28:42 UTC → 09:28:45 UTC'), so the user has to subtract in their head.
findings.evidence: status.ts:107 formatDuration is used only in WorkerInputs.tsx:95 and Assignment.tsx:75/103 for timeouts. NodeDetail.tsx:197 shows checks as start → finish. RunView.tsx:172-173 shows node meta as status · kind · attempt. WorkflowGraph.tsx:109-110 shows status · attempt · executor. Durations derivable from the payloads: skeleton-001 total 56m26s, challenge 11m07s (attempt 3 alone 2m29s), worker game 28m21s (native_started_at 08:50:52 → stop.confirmed_at 09:19:13), verify 10m01s over 3 attempts, candidate about 1m06s, review about 2m10s. skeleton-fixes-001 total 31m49s. Reviewers general 3m49s and coverage 2m04s (launched_at → accepted_at).
findings.user_impact: The user cannot see how long each step took, where the time went (half of skeleton-001 was the worker) or whether something is taking unusually long. This is one of the explicitly listed daily questions.
findings.data_available: events.occurred_at (first and last per node and per attempt), inputs.workers[].launch.native_started_at + stop.confirmed_at, results checks[].started_at/finished_at, reviews reviewers[].launched_at/accepted_at + reviewed_at, summary.created_at/updated_at.
findings.suggestion: Show 'took Xm Ys' on each node in the graph and node list, and a 'Started · Finished · Took' row in the node facts. Add a duration column in the checks list, run duration in the header and run list, and a per-reviewer duration. Add a small phase bar (Gantt strip) under the run header: Challenge 11m | Worker 28m | Verify 10m | Candidate 1m | Review 2m ✗.

findings.problem: The run header cannot tell the user when the run failed or went idle, or what happened most recently. 'Updated' is not last activity, and 'Last event: sequence 26' is a counter that points at an event the UI never displays. Nothing says 'failed at 09:32 in Independent review'.
findings.evidence: RunView.tsx:99-101. server/projects.ts:936 sets updated_at = max(state.updated_at, last event time). In skeleton-001, Updated shows 09:36:07 while the last event is 09:32:32 (#26, a hidden controller PID line) and the actual failure is reviewed_at 09:32:31, so Updated reflects an export rewrite 3.5 minutes after activity stopped. The run list (ProjectsView.tsx:203, 03-fold) shows only 'updated 2026-09-24 09:36:07 UTC · created …': no duration, no failing node, no relative age.
findings.user_impact: While watching live, the user cannot tell whether the run is progressing, idle or dead, or since when. For a failed run they have to find the red node and open it to learn when and why.
findings.data_available: The last event's occurred_at and message, the first failed/paused/awaiting node in the snapshot plus its last event or review.reviewed_at, and summary.created_at.
findings.suggestion: Replace Created/Updated/Last event with one status sentence: 'Failed 09:32 (2 h ago) at Independent review · blocked by general · ran 56m (08:39 → 09:32)'. For a live run: 'Running 23m · now: Launch game worker (working 12m) · last activity 40s ago: <message>'. Use the same one-liner on the run list cards, sorted newest first.

findings.page: All pages that show a time (run list, run header, events, checks, launch receipt, questions, reviewers, challenge)
findings.problem: Every time is rendered as a full ISO date plus seconds in UTC ('2026-09-24 08:39:40 UTC'). There is no local time, no relative time ('3 min ago') and no shortening for same-day times. The user watches from a Mac in another timezone and has to convert every value.
findings.evidence: status.ts:100-104 formatTime returns toISOString(), replacing 'T' with a space and the trailing Z with ' UTC'. It is used in RunView.tsx:99-100, ProjectsView.tsx:203, NodeDetail.tsx:197/351/385/476, WorkerInputs.tsx:139-140/282/288/351, ReviewDetail.tsx:158-159/244 and Challenge.tsx:49. Every event row repeats '2026-09-24' (05-full, 07-c crop). Tests pin the UTC text: tests/project-workflows/inputs.spec.ts:143-155 and guardrails.spec.ts:56/222/231.
findings.user_impact: 'When did it happen' needs mental timezone arithmetic. Relative recency, which matters most for live watching, is missing, and the long strings make event rows wrap, especially at 390px.
findings.data_available: All timestamps are ISO UTC, and the browser knows the local timezone. Nothing new is needed.
findings.suggestion: Render <time dateTime={iso} title='2026-09-24 08:39:40 UTC'>. The primary text is local HH:MM (with date only when it differs from today or the run's start), plus a relative suffix for recent or live items ('09:32 · 2 h ago'). Offer an optional 'UTC' toggle for matching CLI logs and events.jsonl. Update the pinned tests, or set timezoneId: 'UTC' in the Playwright config and assert the title attribute.

findings.page: Review node of print-transport runs (08); approval node (skeleton-fixes-001)
findings.problem: Some nodes that ran and decided the run show 'No events reference this node.' The print-transport review has no start time, no per-reviewer launch time and no duration. The approval node succeeded with no event.
findings.evidence: 08-full (crop 08-b): 'Events for this node: No events reference this node.' under a Blocked verdict. skeleton-001.events.json has no review event. result_…skeleton-001_reviews_1.json has reviewers general and coverage with launched_at null. The only times are general.accepted_at 09:32:31.349 and reviewed_at 09:32:31.411. The superseded coverage reviewer has no time at all. Compare the native review in skeleton-fixes-001 (10-b crop): 9 events, launched_at present. skeleton-fixes-001 approval has status succeeded but no event (sequence 24 is review, 25 is integrate).
findings.user_impact: The failing step of the failed run cannot be placed in time. The user cannot see when review started, how long each reviewer took or when coverage was superseded, and an approval shows no record of when it was granted.
findings.data_available: Approximation from existing data: review start ≈ the candidate's succeeded event (09:30:21.6), end = reviewed_at, which gives about 2m10s. The approval time can be approximated by the integrate event. These should be labelled as inferred ('≈ started after candidate').
findings.suggestion: In the timeline, synthesize inferred spans labelled 'inferred from dependencies' and show reviewed_at as the review's decision row. Needs backend: (1) print-transport review should log running/launched/verdict events and record launched_at per print job; (2) approval should log a status_changed event (automatic approval by the finish policy or a CLI decision) with the actor.

findings.problem: A worker question is shown only deep in the launch node, below the result, all created files and the completion evidence. It has an absolute asked_at but no 'waiting for N min'. The run header, run list and graph never say a worker is waiting on the operator.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:410-414 renders WorkerQuestions after ProducedEvidence and CreatedFiles and after WorkerSignals. In 06-full, 'Questions to the operator' sits at ~19,330px of 19,834 (06-z crop). WorkerInputs.tsx:282 shows 'asked at <UTC>' and :273 says the deadline is paused, but not how long. The contract supports questions[].asked_at/answered_at (contracts/projects/v1.ts:151-157).
findings.user_impact: 'Is a worker waiting on a question, and for how long?' cannot be answered without opening the right launch node and scrolling ~19,000px. A waiting worker burns wall-clock time unnoticed.
findings.data_available: inputs.workers[].questions[] (asked_at, answered_at, answer null means waiting) and completion.status === 'question', polled every 5 s with the inputs.
findings.suggestion: Add a run-level banner and graph-node chip: 'game has waited 14 min for an answer (asked 09:40) — python -m workflow answer …'. In the timeline show question asked/answered rows with their wait duration. Put the waiting question at the top of the launch node.

findings.page: Challenge node (05), candidate node (guardrails), any node whose messages use a lowercase 'attempt'
findings.problem: Event attempt numbers are guessed from message text with a case-sensitive regex. Challenge events and some candidate events all read 'attempt 1' while the graph says attempt 3 or 2, so retries over time cannot be read.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:1067-1069 attemptFromMessage uses /\bAttempt (\d+)\b/, and :1081 defaults to 1. 05-full shows all 7 challenge events as 'attempt 1', including '#3 … Design challenge attempt 2' and '#7 … attempt 3 passed', while the graph and node say attempt 3. '#4 Failed KeyboardInterrupt' is labelled attempt 1 but was attempt 2. Challenge attempt 1 (08:39:42) has no terminal event at all. In workflow-guardrails-001 the candidate snapshot attempt is 2 while events #27/28/30/31 all show attempt 1.
findings.user_impact: The history contradicts the header, so the user cannot tell which attempt failed when, or why there were retries.
findings.data_available: Messages contain 'attempt N' (lowercase) for the challenge. lane_results[].attempt and the packet attempts give the candidate attempts.
findings.suggestion: Make the projection regex case-insensitive and also match 'challenge attempt N'. In the UI, group node history by attempt: 'Attempt 1 · 08:39 · ended without a record', 'Attempt 2 · 08:45-08:46 (46s) · interrupted', 'Attempt 3 · 08:48-08:50 (2m29s) · passed'. Needs backend for full fidelity: raw events should carry a structured attempt (and lane), not only prose.

findings.problem: Only the latest attempt's evidence is viewable. Earlier failed verify attempts, with their check times and failure reasons, are served by the API but never linked. Earlier challenge attempts, including a paused one with its P0/P1 concern, are not served.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:299 fetches only node.result_uri (…/results/game/3). The live API returns 200 for …/skeleton-001/results/game/1 and /game/2 (status failed, VERIFICATION_BLOCKED, checks 09:19:40→09:20:20). 07-c crop events #14/#17 say attempts 1 and 2 failed, but no link opens them. Challenge.tsx:44-45 says 'earlier attempts are kept in the run directory'. skeleton-fixes-001 event #2 'attempt 1 paused … 1 P0/P1 concern(s)' has concerns that are not viewable.
findings.user_impact: The user cannot compare attempts over time (what failed on attempt 1 and what changed by attempt 3) without shelling into the VPS.
findings.data_available: …/results/{lane}/{n} for n < current (verify, candidate lanes). Verify attempt start and end come from the events. Needs backend: challenge-<n>.json per attempt, via an endpoint or an inputs.challenge.history array with decided_at and concerns.
findings.suggestion: Add an attempt switcher or per-attempt rows in the node history: 'Attempt 1 · failed 09:20 (1m07s) · unit, integration: no passing test evidence [open]'. Show the operator repair between attempts as its own row.

findings.page: Two-lane run (13): candidate and launch_controller nodes
findings.problem: Lane-specific events are merged onto shared nodes and lose the lane name, so the history reads as unexplained flips. A lane named 'controller' also collides with the controller process, so controller restarts and errors land on launch_controller.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:341-347 aliases '<lane>' → launch_<lane> and 'candidate_<lane>' → candidate, while :1116 treats raw node 'controller' as the controller process. In workflow-guardrails-001.events.json, candidate reads succeeded 20:22:25 → failed 20:24:50 → succeeded 20:24:52 → failed 20:27:13, all with the identical message 'Combined revision 1ab6b95…' and no lane named. The failing lane (ui, VERIFICATION_BLOCKED) appears only in result candidate_ui/2. launch_controller collects 14 events spanning 54m20s, including 8 'Automatic checkpoint controller PID' rows typed status Running and 4 '[Errno 2] No such file or directory: claude' rows typed Failed. Its last event says Running at 20:27:14 while the node is Succeeded.
findings.user_impact: The two-lane run's chronology is actively misleading: a worker looks like it ran for the whole run and failed four times, and the candidate appears to flip without reason.
findings.data_available: Partial: lane_results[].worker/attempt, result checks timing per lane (candidate_controller 20:18:12→20:22:25, candidate_ui/2 20:25:04→20:27:13).
findings.suggestion: Needs backend: keep the raw node as a 'lane' field (or prefix the message with the lane) in normalized events, and never alias the controller-process node onto a lane. In the UI, show a lane chip on candidate rows ('ui · failed · browser evidence missing') and render the controller's outage window as run-level rows.

findings.problem: For a running worker the UI shows no elapsed time, no deadline and no remaining time, only static absolute launch times at the bottom of the launch page. After the stop, 'Observed state: working' is still shown with no time, and the completion signal has no timestamp.
findings.evidence: WorkerInputs.tsx:130-147 shows the Launch receipt with launch_requested_at and native_started_at absolute. Deadlines are shown only as 'worker 3h · review 1h' (RunView.tsx:125, status.ts:119). skeleton-001.inputs.json has launch.observed_state 'working' while stop.confirmed_at is 09:19:13.53. The completion ('Reported by the worker', WorkerInputs.tsx:318-332) has no time field in the contract (v1.ts:221-238).
findings.user_impact: The user cannot tell how long the worker has been going, when it will time out, or when it signalled completion versus when it was stopped.
findings.data_available: native_started_at + automatic.worker_timeout_seconds (10800) − the sum of question waits (asked_at→answered_at) gives the deadline. Elapsed time is now − native_started_at. Worked time is native_started_at → stop.confirmed_at (28m21s). The review deadline is reviewers[].launched_at + review_timeout_seconds.
findings.suggestion: Show 'Working 12m · deadline 11:50 (2h38m left, paused while a question waits)' on the node, the graph chip and the run status line. After the stop show 'Worked 28m21s (08:50 → 09:19)'. Label observed_state as 'last observed' or hide it after the stop. Needs backend: completion signalled_at and observed_state observed_at.

findings.page: Run page, handoff node (12), guardrails run (13)
findings.problem: Periods of waiting, outages and operator time are not visible. The handoff node shows only the instant of the freeze, not the wait for the worker. Gaps between events (operator investigation, controller down) can only be found by subtracting timestamps across pages.
findings.evidence: 12-full handoff events: #11/#12 both at 10:07:53. The real wait for the completion signal ran from 09:52:10 to 10:07:53 (15m43s). skeleton-001 had a 5m37s operator investigation between #19 09:21:32 and the #20 repair at 09:27:09. workflow-guardrails-001 handoff 'failed' at 19:33:10, 19:42:47, 19:48:29 and 20:03:10 with controller restarts in between; the user had to write this outage window (19:33–20:03) by hand in AI_ROADMAP_REPORT.md:82.
findings.user_impact: Waiting on a human, on the controller or on infrastructure cannot be told apart from agents doing work, so 'when did it go idle and why' is unanswerable.
findings.data_available: Consecutive events' occurred_at, status failed/paused rows, and controller PID rows (restarts).
findings.suggestion: In the timeline, insert gap rows when more than about 2 minutes pass without events, classified by the surrounding events: 'Waiting on worker 15m43s', 'Paused, waiting on operator 5m37s → Repair 1', 'Controller down 9m37s (claude not found) → resumed'. Tint these rows on the phase bar.

findings.page: Run page and run list while polling
findings.problem: Polling every 5 s is silent. A failed poll keeps the old data with no indication, and nothing says 'as of HH:MM:SS'. A remote viewer cannot tell an idle run from a stale page.
findings.evidence: usePoll.ts:4 POLL_INTERVAL_MS=5000. useResource.ts:32 keeps the previous 'ready' value when a poll fails. ProjectsView.tsx:46/52 polls until succeeded or cancelled. No freshness text appears in 03, 04 or 13.
findings.user_impact: When watching from the Mac over the network, the user may trust a stale screen, for example believing a worker is still running after the tunnel dropped.
findings.data_available: Client-side request times and the poll result state. No backend is needed.
findings.suggestion: Add a small pill next to the run status: 'Live · updated 3s ago'. It turns to 'Stale: last refresh 2 min ago — retrying' on poll failures and to 'Finished · not polling' for terminal runs.

findings.problem: The 'Requested at' list in the awaiting-approval notice and the reuse section depend on event types that the projection never produces. A node awaiting a decision therefore never shows since when it has been waiting. Separately, every node page carries an always-empty 'Reuse evidence' block.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:306-307 and 383-387 filter type === 'approval_requested' / 'result_reused'. server/projects.ts:1087 normalizeEvents only emits 'status_changed' or 'log'. 'No reuse evidence recorded…' appears on every node in 05, 07, 08, 10, 11 and 12.
findings.user_impact: 'How long has this been waiting on me?' goes unanswered for approvals, and the always-empty block pushes timing information further down.
findings.data_available: The awaiting node's last status_changed event (occurred_at) and the interrupt in the snapshot.
findings.suggestion: Show 'Awaiting approval since 10:14 (12 min)' using the node's last status event time, and hide 'Reuse evidence' when the export cannot produce it. Needs backend: emit approval_requested / result_reused typed events if they are meant to exist.

findings.problem: The verifier's setup time is invisible, and the candidate has no start event. Check rows give absolute ranges only, so the user cannot see that about 40% of a verify attempt is 'npm ci' or when the candidate began.
findings.evidence: verify_game attempt 3 started 09:28:00.5 (event #23) but the first check started 09:28:42.7 (result game/3), so about 42s of setup is unaccounted for. Attempt 1 had 09:19:13.9 → 09:19:40.6 (27s). The candidate has only a succeeded event (#25 09:30:21), with checks 09:29:41 → 09:30:21. The node page shows 'Graph attempt 1' with no times (11-a crop).
findings.user_impact: Slow verifications cannot be diagnosed (setup or tests?), and the candidate's position in time is unclear.
findings.data_available: The verify node's running event minus the first check's started_at gives setup. Candidate start ≈ the verify succeeded event, or the first check started_at minus setup. inputs.setup[] names the setup command and timeout.
findings.suggestion: On verify and candidate nodes, show a small breakdown: 'Setup (npm ci) 42s · Checks 33s · Total 1m15s', and a duration per check. Needs backend: setup started/finished in the packet, and a candidate 'running' event per lane.

findings.problem: The project and workflow levels have no recency or activity. The two workflow cards are both named 'Feature implementation' and show only revision hashes, so the user has to open each to find the latest or active run.
findings.evidence: 02-project-b-fold shows 'skeleton · 8 nodes · current revision ccdd5a54711d' and 'skeleton-fixes · 8 nodes · current revision 1d261e8e1186'. ProjectsView.tsx:163-170 has no timestamps. The workflowList contract (v1.ts:275-276) carries no run info.
findings.user_impact: There is an extra navigation hop, plus guessing, to answer 'what ran last / what is running now'.
findings.data_available: Derivable with one runs request per workflow (first page is newest first by updated_at, with status, created_at and updated_at). A backend addition would be a latest-run summary in the workflow list to avoid N+1 requests.
findings.suggestion: On each workflow card add 'Last run skeleton-001 · Failed · 2 h ago · 56m'. Sort cards by last activity, and add a 'Running now' section on the Projects root.

findings.problem: Event rows are hard to scan. Each shows '#sequence', the full UTC date and time, the literal type ('status changed'/'log'), a status badge and a redundant 'attempt 1', before the message, which is often a raw revision hash or a comma-joined session list.
findings.evidence: NodeDetail.tsx:474-482. 10-b crop, #24 'status changed · Succeeded · attempt 1 — a8e3ee2a-…, 972ceba4-…'. 07-c crop, #13 '… Attempt 1; revision 5c1a734e71c3312a8d9174f50951e27fcd26d0b7'.
findings.user_impact: Even where history exists, reading it is slow, and the long rows wrap on mobile.
findings.data_available: The same event fields.
findings.suggestion: Use compact rows: time (local, short) · node or lane chip · status dot · humanized message (shorten SHAs to 7 characters, map known messages like 'Awaiting explicit completion signal' to 'waiting for worker to finish'). Put the sequence number and full message in a hover or expander.

findings.problem: Reviewer times are shown as absolute launch and accept times without a duration or deadline, and a superseded reviewer shows no time for when it was stopped.
findings.evidence: ReviewDetail.tsx:156-160 shows 'launched 10:10:13 UTC · file accepted 10:14:02 UTC' (10-a crop). Coverage in skeleton-001 was superseded with launched_at and accepted_at both null. The native stop times exist only as events #22/#23 in skeleton-fixes-001.
findings.user_impact: Which reviewer was slow, or how close a reviewer came to the 1h review deadline, is not visible.
findings.data_available: reviewers[].launched_at/accepted_at, automatic.review_timeout_seconds, and review node log events (native).
findings.suggestion: Show 'general 3m49s · coverage 2m04s' and a deadline for pending reviewers ('deadline 11:10, 56m left'). Add superseded or stopped times in the timeline. Needs backend: a stop time for print or superseded reviewers.

result.questions_by_page:
PROJECTS LIST (01). Is anything running right now? Which project had activity most recently? First screen: NO. Only names and IDs, with no status or time.

PROJECT (02). Which feature or workflow ran last, and how did it end? Is one running? First screen: NO. Two identical 'Feature implementation' cards show only revision hashes, with no run time or status.

WORKFLOW RUN LIST (03, 03-mobile).
- When did the latest run start and end, and how long did it take? PARTIAL: absolute UTC created/updated only, no duration, and 'updated' is not last activity.
- Did it pass, and where did it stop? PARTIAL: a status badge only, no failing node or failure time.
- Is it live, and when did it last change? NO: no relative time and no freshness indicator.

RUN PAGE (04, 09, 13; mobile 04).
- What is active right now? PARTIAL: graph colours only, no 'running for Xm'.
- When did it fail or go idle, and what happened most recently? NO: 'Updated 09:36:07 UTC' is 3.5 minutes after the last activity, and 'Last event: sequence 26' is a number.
- How long did each step take, and the total? NO: no durations anywhere.
- What is the chronology of retries, repairs and controller resumes? NO: there is no run timeline, and node_id-null events (repair, diagnosis, resumes) are never rendered.
- Is a worker waiting on a question, and since when? NO: this is only visible deep inside the launch node.
- Are times in my timezone? NO: UTC only.

NODE PAGES.
- Challenge (05). When did each attempt run, how long did it take, and why was it retried? NO in the first screen. Events are at ~1,950 of 3,655px, all mislabelled 'attempt 1', with no durations. Earlier attempts' concerns are not viewable.
- Launch worker (06). When did the worker start, how long has it worked or did it work, what is the deadline, when did it signal completion or stop? NO. The launch receipt, stop line and events are at ~19,300-19,800px of a 19,834px page. Elapsed time, deadline and completion time are not shown, and the observed state 'working' is stale.
- Handoff (12). How long did we wait for the worker? NO. Only the freeze instant is shown, although the page fits in one screen.
- Verify (07, 07-mobile). Which attempt failed when, how long did checks and setup take, and what changed between attempts? NO. Check ranges are at ~3,100px, events at ~4,400px (desktop) and ~8,800px (mobile). There are no durations, and earlier attempts' results are not linked even though the API serves them.
- Candidate (11). When did it start, how long did it take, and which lane failed when? NO. There is no start event, check ranges are below the fold, and in the two-lane run the lane-less flipping events are confusing.
- Review (08 print, 10 native). When did review start, how long did each reviewer take, and when was the verdict? PARTIAL. 'Reviewed at' and the reviewer launch and accept times are just below the fold. The print review has 'No events reference this node' and no launch times, and there are no durations or deadline.
- Approval/Integrate. When was it approved or integrated? Approval: NO ('No events'). Integrate: one event at the bottom.

ASSIGNMENT TAB (14). How much time was the worker given, and what were the timeouts? YES: timeouts per check and setup and deadlines are listed. It carries no chronology, which is fine for its purpose.
result.notes:
TIMESTAMP INVENTORY (what the API exposes → where the UI renders it today):
- summary.created_at/updated_at → run header 'Created/Updated' (RunView.tsx:99-100) and run list card (ProjectsView.tsx:203). updated_at = max(export updated_at, last event time) (server/projects.ts:936), so it can trail activity.
- snapshot.last_sequence → 'Last event: sequence N' (no time or message).

A TIMELINE THAT CAN BE BUILT PURELY FROM EXISTING DATA (skeleton-001 as the example; times in UTC here, local in the UI):
Header: 'Failed at Independent review · 09:32 (blocked by general, 1 P1) · ran 56m (08:39→09:32) · last activity 09:32'.
Phase bar: Challenge 11m07s (3 attempts) | Worker game 28m21s | Handoff instant | Verify 10m01s (3 attempts incl. 5m37s operator repair) | Candidate ≈1m06s | Review ≈2m10s ✗.
Rows: 08:39:42 Challenge attempt 1 started · 08:45:55 re-pinned → attempt 2 · 08:46:41 attempt 2 interrupted (KeyboardInterrupt, 46s) · 08:48:20 attempt 3 · 08:50:49 passed (2m29s, 8 P2) · 08:50:52 worker game started (native) · 08:50:55 controller resumed · [gap 28m: worker working] · 09:19:13 worker stopped, snapshots frozen · 09:19:13 verify attempt 1 → 09:20:20 failed (1m07s; unit/integration: no test evidence) · 09:20:23 attempt 2 → 09:21:30 failed (1m07s) · 09:21:32 DIAGNOSIS 'failed identically… lane repair (RUNBOOK)' · [gap 5m37s: operator] · 09:27:09 Repair 1 by operator (reporter for Vitest) · 09:28:00 controller resumed, attempt 3 → 09:29:15 passed (1m15s: setup 42s + checks 33s) · 09:29:41–09:30:21 candidate checks passed · ≈09:30:21 review started (inferred) · 09:32:31 general blocked (1 P1), coverage superseded → run failed.
Derivation rules: node span = first→last status event, or dependency end → reviewed_at/stop.confirmed_at when events are missing (label these 'inferred'). Attempt spans come from events once the lowercase 'attempt' parse is fixed. Worker span = native_started_at→stop.confirmed_at. Question wait = asked_at→answered_at or now. Worker deadline = native_started_at + worker_timeout_seconds + question waits. Reviewer deadline = launched_at + review_timeout_seconds. Gaps over about 2 minutes between events become labelled gap rows. Earlier verify attempts link to .../results/{lane}/{n} (verified live: game/1 and game/2 return 200).

BACKEND GAPS (events or fields needed for full fidelity):
1. Print-transport review: no events and reviewers[].launched_at null. The controller should log launch/verdict per print job.
2. Approval: no event when it succeeds (automatic finish or CLI). It should log the decision and the actor.
3. Candidate: no 'running' event, and per-lane events are aliased to 'candidate' without the lane.
4. The controller-process raw node 'controller' collides with a lane named 'controller' (server/projects.ts:341-347 vs :1116).
5. Attempt parsing is case-sensitive (server/projects.ts:1067-1069). The server-side fix is cheap, but a structured attempt and lane on raw events is better.
6. Worker completion has no signalled_at, and launch.observed_state has no observed_at.
7. Earlier challenge attempts (challenge-<n>.json) are not served, including a paused attempt's P0/P1 concerns.
8. Verify packet lacks setup started/finished.
9. No run-level terminal event ('run failed at node X'). A last_activity_at distinct from export rewrite time would make the header honest.
10. Event types approval_requested/result_reused/result_published are declared in the contract but never produced by normalizeEvents (server/projects.ts:1087), so the UI sections that depend on them are always empty.

result.notes:
Method: I read every fold screenshot directly. For the tall -full PNGs I cropped them into 1,500px slices with a small pure-Python PNG decoder, because the full images downscale too far to read. The slices are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux/work/ (e.g. 06-04500.png means launch page y 4,500-6,000), and the script is work/crop.py. Page heights come from the PNG headers; y positions are read from the slices at 1440px width and are approximate (±30px). Nothing in the repo was edited, and no tests or servers were run.

The live API was used read-only: 4 workflows, each with exactly 1 run, all named 'Feature implementation'. results/game/1 and /2 for skeleton-001 return 200 with the failed attempts' checks and error, so earlier attempts can be shown without backend work.

Root cause for the naming problem: workflow/export_state.py:84 returns {"name": "Feature implementation", …}.

Constraints for redesign (testids pinned by tests/project-workflows/*.spec.ts): run-node-list with [data-node-id] children (lanes, guardrails, projects specs); graph-legend with 3 li carrying data-executor (clarity.spec.ts:105-109); node-status-meaning containing 'not workflow completion' (projects.spec.ts:172); node-hint (projects.spec.ts:162,179); projects-info containing 'Read-only' (projects.spec.ts:81); reuse-none/reuse-list and node-events/events-none must be visible (projects.spec.ts:232-256); file-findings-none exact text (clarity.spec.ts:268); tab-assignment/tab-run; run-inputs-facts (7 uses). A compacted design can keep these testids on smaller elements, such as tooltips or collapsed sections, but tests asserting toBeVisible will need updating if content moves behind disclosures.

Truthfulness intent from the earlier slices to preserve in compact form: executor marks (PRD_VIEWER_CLARITY §4.3), 'worker succeeded ≠ workflow complete', and the read-only / CLI-only actions.

Suggested IA direction, one page per question:
- Runs home (all projects): runs newest first, with feature title, status, current or failed step, age, duration and a needs-you flag.
- Run page: a 'Now' banner (step, reason, next command), a timeline with durations, a compact fitted graph, and collapsed run details.
- Node view: full width, sticky step strip with prev/next, sub-tabs with counts (Overview/Checks/Screenshots/Files/Findings/Questions/Task/Events), and an attempt switcher.
- Assignment: routed, per lane, decisions collapsed.

Backend asks, collected:
1. Feature title as definition.name, or a feature_title field.
2. An attention field on RunSummary (waiting questions, awaiting approval, failed node).
3. A copyable next-step command, or the unredacted run path.
4. Per-node attempt result URIs.
5. Controller event fixes: review events for print transport, PID checkpoint as a node-less log, and a reason on candidate failure events.

result.notes:
How the heights were measured: y positions come from reading the 1500px slices already in scratchpad/ux/work/ (06-*, 07-*, 07m-*, 08-*, 10-*, 11-*, 12-*, 14-*), cross-checked against the payloads. Read-only checks against the live API:
- GET …/skeleton-001/results/game/1 and /2 return 200, so earlier verification attempts are served; attempt 1 failed with every check at exit 0.
- The skeleton-fixes-001 review patch artifact has 21 per-file diffs.
- log-77 is the npm ci setup log.

I read one packet.json read-only under ~/.local/state (nothing was modified). Its evidence.checks[] already records per-check id, test counts and scenario→screenshot_artifact_id, and gate.reasons is an array. The server drops both when it publishes the strict WorkerResult (server/projects.ts ~1215-1235). A small additive optional field would feed the check table, the scenario-captioned thumbnails and the per-check gate reasons.

Height budget for launch_game (19,834px): header ~260, result facts and summary ~590, assumptions ~670, files ~15,440 (71 file stubs ≈10,650 plus 6 rendered .md ≈4,600), worker report repeated ~1,560, receipt/task/reuse/events ~520.

Height budget for verify_game (4,965px): worker summary and assumptions ~1,250 before the Gate, checks ~650, screenshots ~1,070, events ~440.

Tests that lock the current layout and would need updating:
- clarity.spec.ts 'created-file-rendered' asserts Markdown files render inline by default.
- clarity.spec.ts 'output-first-task-collapsed' asserts result and files come before the task.
- clarity.spec.ts 'verify-shows-checks-not-files'.
- Keep the existing data-testids: created-file, captured-file, file-rendered, file-source, gate-outcome, deferred-checks, checks-list, screenshots, worker-completion, task-details, node-events, finding, filter-reviewer, group-by-*.

The honesty requirements from the earlier slices can stay; they only need to be said once:
- 'worker Succeeded ≠ workflow completion' as a badge tooltip.
- 'as signalled by the session, not verified' as a small tag.
- The read-only and CLI wording as a copyable command chip.

Out of lens but noticed: the run page fold is taken up by run facts, graph and legend, and log events with node_id null (e.g. 'Repair 1 applied', 'failed identically on attempts 1 and 2') appear on no node. The run-page and timeline lenses should cover both.

findings.page: Graph, run header, run list, launch node (06)
findings.problem: A worker that is waiting on a question, or that 'needs attention in its pane', is displayed as 'Running', the same as a working worker. The controller records these as 'interactive' events, and the server maps interactive to running. The question text and its answer command reach the viewer only as an event with a blue Running badge. That event sits in the 'Events for this node' list at the very bottom of the launch node, which is about 19,700 px down in 06-full. The 'Questions to the operator' section (≈y 19,300) reads inputs.workers[].questions from run-state.json. That file is re-exported only after graph steps (pipeline.advance), not during the wait_handoffs loop, so during a live wait it can still say 'No questions were recorded for this worker.' result.notes:
What I used: all fold/full screenshots (plus the existing crops in scratchpad/ux/work/06-*.png and 10-a.png), the API payloads in scratchpad/ux/api, and a live read-only GET of a new running run, project-b/duel-core/duel-core-001, at 11:17:57Z. I saved it to scratchpad/ux/work/live/{detail,events,inputs}.json. Its snapshot: challenge succeeded on attempt 2 after a P1 pause (11:08→11:10), launch_duel running since 11:12:58, deadline 3 h, 'updated' frozen at 11:13:02. There is no screenshot of that run page because I ran no Playwright. The live-state claims come from the code: RunView/NodeDetail rendering, server/projects.ts:373 mapping interactive→running, and questions read only from the export.

CLI commands for a 'Next step' box, verified against `.venv/bin/python -m workflow <cmd> --help` and workflow/RUNBOOK.md:
- `automatic "$RUN" --live`: resume after an interruption or after a repair.
- `resume "$RUN" [--accept-challenge REASON]`: for a paused design challenge.
- `answer "$RUN" <lane> "<text>"`: answer a worker's question.
- `repair "$RUN" <lane[,lane]> --workspace | --commit SHA --reason ...`: a code fix before review, after an identical failure.
- `retry "$RUN" --phase worker|candidate --node <lane>`: an interrupted check step.
- `approve "$RUN" --bundle-sha256 <hash>`: manual runs.
- `status` / `export "$RUN"`.
- After a review block, the RUNBOOK says fixing findings needs a new run (RUNBOOK.md:244, 287).

Constraint: the server redacts absolute paths to <path> (server/projects.ts:75), so copy-paste-ready commands need a backend decision on exposing a run-directory handle.

Honesty requirements to keep while trimming wording:
- Never call a worker's success workflow completion.
- A viewer never approves anything.
- Idle is not acceptance.

These can live in one tooltip or legend instead of three footnotes per page.

Out of lens, but seen: the Assignment tab and created-files length (the launch page is about 20,000 px) are covered by other lenses. The mobile node deep link opens far above the node detail.

Possible backend bug worth a separate check: a lane named 'controller' swallows controller events (server/projects.ts:341-347). That also feeds projectSnapshot's lastEvent for launch_controller, which could mis-state the node as running while the handoff is open.

result.name: Answer-first run triage
result.thesis: Every Projects page should answer the operator's question in its top block, before it shows any evidence. A run page opens with a "Now" banner computed from existing data: the step where the run is or stopped, why in one line, when (local time plus how long ago), and the exact CLI command to run next with a Copy button. Below it come one card per lane (worker, verify, candidate, findings), then a step timeline with durations, which also serves as the node list. Deeper evidence (checks, logs, screenshots, files, findings, task) sits one click away in URL-addressable node tabs. One pure module, contracts/projects/triage.ts, does the classification and timing. The browser uses it first. The server reuses it later to give run lists the same headline, so the runs list becomes a dashboard sorted by what needs the operator.

result.timeline:
**Built client-side from fields that already exist.** The pure functions live in `contracts/projects/triage.ts`: `nodeSpans`, `attemptSpans`, `runSpan`, `gaps`. Their inputs are `events[]` (occurred_at, node_id, status, attempt, message), `inputs.workers[].launch.native_started_at` and `launch_requested_at`, `stop.confirmed_at`, `questions[].asked_at` and `answered_at`, `inputs.challenge.decided_at`, `max_verification_attempts`, `automatic.worker_timeout_seconds` and `review_timeout_seconds`, `results.checks[].started_at` and `finished_at`, `review.reviewed_at`, `reviewers[].launched_at` and `accepted_at`, and `summary.created_at`.

**Span rules per kind** (a value derived from dependencies rather than an event is prefixed "≈" and carries the title "inferred: no event recorded"):
- **Challenge.** Runs from its first event to its succeeded or paused event. Tries come from the message (`/attempt (\d+)/i`, a client workaround until server/projects.ts:1067 is made case-insensitive). skeleton-001 gives: try 1 08:39:42 (no terminal record), try 2 08:45:55–08:46:41 (46s, interrupted), try 3 08:48:20–08:50:49 (2m29s, passed).
- **Worker.** Runs from `native_started_at` (or `launch_requested_at`) to `stop.confirmed_at`, or to now while running (08:50:52 → 09:19:13 = 28m21s). Question waits (asked → answered, or now) are drawn hatched on the bar. The deadline is `native_started_at + worker_timeout + Σ question waits`.
- **Handoff.** Its events, with failed events as ✗ markers. For guardrails-001 this shows four failures between 19:33 and 20:03.
- **Verification.** One sub-span per try, from the "Attempt N" running event to the next terminal event: ✗ 09:19:13–09:20:20 (1m07s), ✗ 09:20:23–09:21:30, ✓ 09:28:00–09:29:15 (1m15s). Setup time is the first check's `started_at` minus the running event (42s). The ⚒ repair marker comes from the run-level "Repair 1 applied" event and the paused event #20.
- **Candidate.** Starts ≈ at the last verify success (or the first lane check's `started_at` once lane results load) and ends at its last status event. Guardrails rows get lane chips taken from lane results, e.g. "ui ✗ browser evidence".
- **Review.** Native transport: first running event → terminal event. Print transport: ≈ candidate end → `review.reviewed_at`. Each reviewer runs `launched_at` → `accepted_at`, or shows "not recorded".
- **Approval and integrate.** Their event when there is one, otherwise "≈ with integrate" or "no event".
- **Run.** Runs from `created_at` to the last terminal evidence (09:32:31 for skeleton-001, so "ran 53m", not `updated_at` 09:36:07, which is an export rewrite). "Last activity" is the time of the last event (not the controller PID line).

**Steps view** (the overview default, `run-node-list`): one row per node in definition order. Columns are glyph and status, label link, start (local HH:MM), duration, a bar on a shared axis from run start to finish (or now), tries markers (✗✗⚒✓), and a one-line outcome. Bars are CSS (`left` and `width` in %) and `aria-hidden`; the times are in the text. A running bar extends to "now" and ticks with `useNow(5 s)`.

**Log view:** every event in time order, including the node_id null ones. Each row shows local time (HH:MM:SS), a node or "run" chip, a status dot, and a humanised message (SHAs cut to 7 characters, "Awaiting explicit completion signal" becomes "waiting for the worker to signal completion"). The sequence number and the full message are in an expander. Consecutive "Automatic checkpoint controller PID" lines collapse into one "Controller (re)started" marker, hidden unless "Show controller logs" is on. Gaps of more than 2 minutes become labelled rows based on what was open: "worker working 28m", "paused, waiting on the operator 5m37s → Repair 1", "controller down 31m ([Errno 2] 'claude' not found ×3)". Filters: [All] [Problems]. The order is chronological, newest first while the run is live. A node's Events tab reuses this component, filtered to the node plus run-level events inside its span, so the repair shows on Verify game.

**Times everywhere:** a `<time dateTime={iso} title="2026-09-24 09:32:31 UTC">` element. It shows local HH:MM, adds the date when the day differs from today, and adds a relative suffix ("2 h ago") for last-activity and live items. A Local/UTC toggle is kept in localStorage (a per-viewer convenience) for matching CLI logs. Durations use a new `formatSpan` (3s, 1m07s, 28m21s, 2h05m). Check rows read "typecheck · 3s · exit 0". Attempts use one term: "try N of max" for verify and candidate (`max_verification_attempts`), and "N tries" on the challenge. A pending node shows "—", never "attempt 0".
result.live_and_next_action:
**Classifier.** `classifyRun()` in triage.ts takes the snapshot, definition, events, inputs, review and failing lane results. It returns `{situation, focusNodeId, headline, reason, at, attention, next}`. The first matching rule wins:
1. **Question**: a lane has `questions[].answer === null`, or `completion.status === 'question'`, or its newest event matches `/^Worker (\S+) asked question (\d+)/` with no later "working" event for that lane. The last case covers the live wait, where run-state.json is not re-exported. Headline: "Waiting on you: game asked question 2 of 3 · 14 min ago · deadline paused". Next: `python -m workflow answer <run> game "<your answer>"`.
2. **Awaiting approval** (a node with status awaiting_approval): "Awaiting your approval since 10:14 (12 min)", where the time is the node's last status event. Next: `python -m workflow approve <run> --bundle-sha256 <review.bundle_sha256>`.
3. **Challenge paused**: "Paused: design challenge found 1 P1". Next: edit the feature files, then `python -m workflow resume <run>`, or `resume <run> --accept-challenge "<reason>"`.
4. **Interrupted, or Claude Code unavailable**: a paused or failed event whose message matches `interrupted|exit 75|Errno`. Next: fix Claude Code, then `python -m workflow automatic <run> --live`.
5. **Identical failure before review**: a node-less "failed identically" log, or two consecutive failed events or lane errors with the same reason, and no review recorded. Headline: "Stopped at Verify combined candidate (try 2 of 3) · lane ui: Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown". Next: `python -m workflow repair <run> ui --workspace`, then `python -m workflow automatic <run> --live` (RUNBOOK "Blocked after freeze").
6. **Check failed with tries left**: "the supervisor retries by itself". If the controller is stopped: `retry <run> --phase worker|candidate --node <lane>`, then `automatic <run> --live`.
7. **Review blocked**: "Blocked at Independent review · general: 1 P1 open — <first sentence>". Next: a new run, `python -m workflow launch <feature> --run-id <feature>-00N --automatic --live`, run from the target repo (RUNBOOK §5 "Fixing findings means a new run").
8. **Running**: "Running · Launch duel worker · working 5m of 3h (deadline 14:12, 2h55m left) · last activity 40 s ago". Nothing is needed; an optional `status <run>` is offered.
9. **Succeeded**: "Integrated ee74298 into feature/skeleton-fixes/skeleton-fixes-001 (not pushed) · 32m · review approved, 2 open P2". The command is labelled "optional, outside the workflow".
10. **Unknown failure**: the latest failing event message shown verbatim, the step link, and `status <run>`.

**Where it surfaces**
- The Now banner (`run-now`, `data-situation`) at the top of the run overview.
- A one-line run bar on every node page.
- The node header of the focus node (`node-verdict`, with `awaiting-notice` kept for awaiting nodes).
- The graph node (`data-attention`, a ⚑ glyph, amber).
- The step chip.
- The lane card.
- The run rows and a "Needs you" count on the dashboard, once `glance.attention` exists.
- `document.title` gets a "⚑ " prefix while a question or approval waits, so a background Mac tab shows it.
- Screen readers: the existing ProjectsView announcer speaks the headline only when it changes, never on every poll. The banner is not an aria-live region.

**Next step box** (`next-step`): one sentence of why, the RUNBOOK section name, and the command in `<code>` (`user-select: all`, scrolls sideways inside its own box). The Copy button's visible text is only "Copy" or "Copied", so `expectNoExecutionControls` still passes. Placeholders are shown as `<…>`. The box states once: "Run in your terminal — this viewer never changes a run." `<run>` is filled from the new `RunDetail.run_dir` (home-relative). Until that field exists, the command uses `"$RUN"` and names the run directory pattern.

**Liveness.** `useResource` records `lastOk` and `failing`. Refresh becomes a background reload that keeps the data and scroll position (useResource.ts:22-23: refreshToken moves from `base` to `token`). The LivePill shows "● Live · updated 3 s ago", "▲ Connection lost · showing data from 11:14:02 · retrying" (announced once), or "○ Finished · not polling". The Refresh button shows a busy state. The running glyph pulses only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

**Wording.** Status is worded by cause ("Blocked by review", "Paused: design challenge", "Waiting on you"). The generic "Marked retryable by the producer" line is removed (server/projects.ts:1235 hard-codes `retryable: true`) and replaced by the attempt and next-step logic.

The API already serves both (200 for game/1 and game/2). A failed attempt opens on its error and rejected checks.

result.name: Run Story: a timeline-first workflow viewer
result.thesis:
A run happens in time, so the run page shows it in time order. The first screen answers three things at a glance:
1. A **Now banner**: where the run is or where it stopped, why, since when, and the CLI command to run next.
2. A **Steps strip**: the pinned graph as status chips with durations. It fits the page width, so there is no inner horizontal scroll.
3. A **Run timeline**: every step attempt, retry, repair, controller restart, question and idle gap, with local times and durations. This includes the events with no node (node_id null) that the viewer hides today.

Each timeline row opens a full-width node view. The view starts with the node's own verdict, timing and tries. Its evidence sits behind a section index with counts (Checks 5 · Screenshots 2 · Files 77 · Findings 4 …), instead of one column up to 20,000px tall.

Almost everything comes from data the run page already loads (events, snapshot, inputs, review) through one pure `buildTimeline()`. Three small server additions add status to the list pages, make run paths copyable, and fix how events are projected.

result.timeline:
**Model.** `src/projects/timeline.ts` exports a pure `buildTimeline({ definition, snapshot, events, inputs, review, now })`. It returns:

```
{
  runStart,
  runEnd | null,
  spans: Span[],       // one per node try: nodeId, label, kind, attempt, attemptsOf, start, end, startSource, endSource, status, outcome, live
  markers: Marker[],   // diagnosis | repair | controller | controllerError | question | answer | log, with a time and the humanized message
  gaps: Gap[],         // from, to, ms, kind: operator | controllerDown | idle
  byNode: Map<nodeId, Span[]>
}
```

It is unit-tested with trimmed copies of the three live payloads. The run page already loads everything it needs:
- `events[]`: sequence, occurred_at, node_id, attempt, status, message.
- `snapshot.nodes[]`: status, attempt, result_uri, lane_results.
- `definition.nodes[]`: label, kind, depends_on (used to infer start times).
- `inputs.workers[]`:
  - `launch.native_started_at` / `launch_requested_at`
  - `stop.confirmed_at`
  - `questions[].asked_at` / `answered_at`
  - `completion.status`
- other `inputs` fields:
  - `challenge.attempts` and `decided_at`
  - `max_verification_attempts`
  - `automatic.worker_timeout_seconds` and `review_timeout_seconds`
- One review result, fetched only once the review node is no longer pending: reviewed_at, reviewers[].launched_at / accepted_at / status.
- The node view adds `checks[].started_at` / `finished_at` from the result it already loads, for the setup-versus-checks split.

**Derivation rules** (each rule carries a source tag, which is shown in the tooltip):
1. **Try number.** Re-read the try from the message with `/\battempt (\d+)/i` before falling back to `event.attempt`. The server's parser only matches a capital "Attempt" (`server/projects.ts:1068`), which is why every challenge event says "attempt 1" today.
2. **Controller noise.** A message matching `Automatic checkpoint controller PID N` is a controller marker wherever it lands. In guardrails it lands on `launch_controller` as "running" (see B4). A `[Errno …]` failure on a node that later succeeded is a controller-error marker.
3. **Spans.** A `running` event opens a span for that node and try. A terminal status (succeeded, failed, paused, cancelled) closes it. A new try opening while one is still open closes the old one as "ended without a record": challenge try 1, 08:39:42 → 08:45:55.
4. **Receipts.**
   - Worker spans use `native_started_at` → `stop.confirmed_at` (08:50:52 → 09:19:13 = 28m21s). The source is shown as "from receipts".
   - A review without events uses `reviewed_at` as its end. Its start is the latest `launched_at`, otherwise the end of the step it depends on, marked "≈ … inferred" (09:30:21 → 09:32:31, ≈2m10s).
   - A candidate without a running event starts at the end of the step it depends on (inferred): 09:29:15 → 09:30:21.
   - An approval without events is an instant at the integrate event's time (inferred).
5. **Run-level events** (node_id null).
   - `failed identically` becomes a highlighted **diagnosis** row.
   - `^Repair (\d+)` becomes a **repair** row, with the snapshot and files from the node's paused event (#20).
   - Anything else becomes a plain log row.
6. **Gaps.** A stretch of more than 120 s with no open span becomes a gap row, classified by what surrounds it:
   - after a diagnosis or failure and before a repair or resume: **operator time** (skeleton-001: 5m37s, 09:21:32 → 09:27:09)
   - after controller errors and before a controller start: **controller not running** (guardrails-001: 19:33 → 19:34, 19:42 → 19:47, 19:48 → 19:55, 20:03 → 20:04)
   - otherwise: **no activity**
   A worker that is working is a span, not a gap.
7. **Questions.** One row per `asked_at` ("game asked question 2 · waited 5m") and per `answered_at`. While `answer === null` the row is live ("waiting 4m, deadline paused"). If the export is stale, an `asked question N` event message without a later answer event serves as a fallback.
8. **Run span.** It runs from `created_at` to the last non-controller activity, not to `updated_at`. For skeleton-001 the page shows 52m51s ending 09:32:31, instead of "Updated 09:36:07".

**Display.**
- Rows are `<li data-testid="timeline-row" data-kind="span|marker|gap|question" data-node-id data-attempt data-status>`. Span rows are links to `/nodes/<n>/attempts/<k>`. Each shows local clock time (HH:MM), a status glyph and word, the label, "try k of N", a one-line humanized outcome, a duration, and a bar.
- The bar is a CSS track. Its left is (start − runStart)/total, its width is the duration/total, minimum 2px, and it is `aria-hidden`. Overlapping lanes show as parallel bars (guardrails: two workers from 19:32:57 to 20:08).
- Inferred values show "≈" plus the source in a tooltip. Times use `<time dateTime title="2026-09-24 09:19:13 UTC">`. A relative age is added when under 24 h or while the run is live.
- A Local/UTC toggle is remembered per viewer in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch. It helps when matching events.jsonl.
- Durations read `46s`, `2m29s`, `28m21s`, `1h05m`. Humanized messages shorten SHAs to 7 characters, and phrases are mapped, e.g. "Awaiting explicit completion signal; idle is not acceptance" → "Waiting for the worker's completion signal (idle is not acceptance)". The full message and sequence number are in the row's title and an expander.
- The order is oldest first, with a remembered "Newest first" toggle. The live span sits at the end: its bar grows to now and it shows `working 12m · deadline 11:50 (2h38m left)`.
- The controller-log toggle hides PID rows by default and shows their count.

**Reuse on other surfaces.**
- The Steps strip shows each node's total (first start → last end) and `↻n` when there were retries.
- The run header shows the total.
- Run rows show age and duration.
- The node view's try strip is `byNode(nodeId)`, and its History section (`node-events`) is the same row component filtered to that node, plus the raw events behind an expander.
- The verify header shows the setup/checks split: attempt start → first `check.started_at` → last `finished_at` (42s + 33s).
- Reviewers show `accepted_at − launched_at` (general 3m49s, coverage 2m04s) and, while pending, time left against `review_timeout_seconds`.
- "Awaiting approval since 10:14 (12 min)" uses the node's last status event.

**Terms.** "try k of N" for verification and candidate, where N is `max_verification_attempts`. "try k" for the challenge. No try count on worker, handoff or pending nodes. "Repair n" for operator repairs. The phrasings "Graph attempt" and "(graph node attempt is 1)" are removed.

**Now banner** (`src/projects/NowBanner.tsx`, testids `run-now`, `now-reason`, `now-command`, `copy-command`). `deriveNow()` in `nextStep.ts` picks one situation, in this priority order:
1. **Waiting on you: a question.**
   - Triggers: `inputs.workers[].questions` has one with `answer === null`, or `completion.status === 'question'`, or an `asked question N` event with no later answer.
   - Shows "? game asked question 2 · 4 min ago · deadline paused", the question text, and `python -m workflow answer "$RUN" game "<your answer>"`.
   - The strip chip gets a `?` badge (`data-attention="question"`), and the run row moves to *Needs you*.
2. **Paused.**
   - A challenge with a P0/P1: "Paused: design challenge found 1 P1; no worker launched". Commands: `python -m workflow resume "$RUN"` after revising the feature files, or `… resume "$RUN" --accept-challenge "<reason>"`.
   - A repair or an interrupt: `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live`.
3. **Failed.** The focus is the failed node (the first in definition order, ties broken by the latest event).
   - The reason comes from, in order: the review verdict plus blocking findings, the failing lane's `error.message` (the only case with extra fetches, one or two lane results, and only when the candidate failed), or the last status event message.
   - Mapping:
     - A diagnosis marker "failed identically" gives `python -m workflow repair "$RUN" <lane> --workspace`, then `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` (RUNBOOK "Blocked after freeze: repair a lane").
     - A review block gives "fixed in a new run" and `python -m workflow launch <new-feature> --automatic --live` (RUNBOOK: "after review started, create a new run").
     - A controller `[Errno …]` gives "Controller could not run claude; fix the environment, then `automatic "$RUN" --live`".
     - Anything else gives "No known next step matched" plus a RUNBOOK section link. The viewer never guesses a command.
4. **Awaiting approval.** "Waiting for your approval since 10:14 (12 min)" and `python -m workflow approve "$RUN" --bundle-sha256 <review.bundle_sha256>`. The hash is filled in from the review result.
5. **Running.**
   - Shows the active node or nodes: "Launch duel worker · working 5m · deadline 14:12 (2h55m left)". The deadline is `native_started_at + worker_timeout_seconds` + paused question time.
   - Adds "Last activity 11:13 (4 min ago): Waiting for the worker's completion signal".
   - Offers an optional attach command: `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one "$RUN" --node duel`.
   - For a review, it shows per-reviewer elapsed time and time left.
6. **Succeeded.** "Integrated ee74298 into feature/skeleton-fixes/skeleton-fixes-001 · not pushed · 31m50s · review approved, 2 open P2 [view]". The source is the integrate event plus `inputs.source_branch`. There is no workflow command, and pushing is left to the operator.
7. **Cancelled or pending:** one plain line.

**Commands.** Commands are always labelled "Likely next step (from the RUNBOOK)" and link to the RUNBOOK section. They use `"$RUN"`, the RUNBOOK's own convention.
- With B3, a `RUN=<runs_root>/<run_id>` line with its own Copy button makes each command paste-ready.
- Without B3, a small `What is $RUN?` disclosure explains "the run directory: this workflow's runs_root/<run id> in the project registry".
- The honesty clause lives in one place, the banner: "Run commands in your terminal; this viewer never changes a run".
- `run-status-meaning` becomes a short cause-aware clause that keeps the tested words: "…The workflow did not complete." for failed, "not complete until you approve it in the CLI" for awaiting approval.
- The Copy button's text is only "Copy" (its aria-label is "Copy command"). So `expectNoExecutionControls` (support.ts:36) still passes.
- Clipboard failure falls back to selecting the `<code>`.

**Focus node on node pages.** When the viewed node is the Now focus, its header repeats the reason and the command. The retryable wording ("Marked retryable by the producer") is replaced with "try 2 of 3 · failed identically → repair" when a diagnosis exists.

**Liveness** (`LiveStatus.tsx`, `live-status`). `useResource` returns `meta { settledAt, lastError, inFlight }`, and `useNow(1000)` renders the ages. States:
- "● Live · updated 3 s ago"
- amber "Not updating · showing data from 11:14:02 · retrying" after a failed poll (today a failed poll is silent, useResource.ts:30-34)
- "Finished · not polling" for succeeded or cancelled runs
- "Paused while this tab is hidden"

With B1 it adds "controller running (PID 3373084)", or "controller not running — the run will not advance", which adds `automatic "$RUN" --live` to the Now banner.

**Refresh.** Header Refresh becomes a background reload: `refreshToken` moves from useResource's `base` to its `token`, so the page no longer blanks, the scroll position and tab survive, and the pill shows "Refreshing…".

result.risks:
- **Inferred or heuristic times.** Some start times are inferred (review, candidate, approval), and parsing the try from message text is fragile. Mitigation:
  - Every inferred value shows "≈" and its source.
  - The heuristics live in one pure module with unit tests on the real payloads.
  - B4 and B5 remove most of them later.
  - A timeline row never claims more than the events do. An open span with no terminal event reads "ended without a record".
- **Wrong next step.** A next-step suggestion could be wrong. Mitigation:
  - It shows only when a situation from the table matches exactly; otherwise it says "No known next step matched" and links the RUNBOOK section.
  - It is always worded "Likely next step (from the RUNBOOK)".
  - The table in nextStep.ts is reviewed against the RUNBOOK and the CLI `--help` whenever the controller changes.
- **Paths in commands.** Without B3, commands contain `"$RUN"`, which the operator must set. Exposing `run_dir` weakens the redaction policy, so it stays opt-in per workflow.
- **Local times.** The CLI and events.jsonl are in UTC. Mitigation: every time's tooltip carries UTC, and a remembered Local/UTC toggle is available.
- **Stale export during the handoff wait.** Mitigation: the question banner falls back to events, and B1 counts both sources. Fully live questions still need B5.
- **Test churn.** About 15 assertions in 5 specs change, and scenario ids must be added to policy.json. Doing it slice by slice keeps each PR reviewable. Keeping testids on their new elements avoids a rewrite of the harness.
- **Losing the SVG DAG.** An unusual DAG, for example with skip-level edges, could read less clearly in a column-grid strip. The overlay still draws every edge, and `layoutDag` stays the single source for columns.
- **Re-renders.** Polling every 5 s re-renders the timeline on every tick. `buildTimeline` is memoized on the last event sequence plus the identities of the snapshot and inputs, and `useNow` ticks only while the run is live.
- **Fan-out on /projects.** It grows as the number of workflows grows; B2 caps it.
- **Changed UI habits.** The operator's links to `/nodes/<n>` keep working. Assignment and tries get new URLs, and the old routes still resolve.

result.name: Pinned Pipeline + Tabbed Inspector
result.thesis: Every run page has two panes. The first is a pipeline band that is always on screen, fits the page width, and is also the step list. The second is an inspector below it that answers questions in the same order everywhere: Summary (what happened, why, what do I type next), Timeline (when and how long), Evidence (proof), Inputs (what was asked). The run itself is the default subject; a step replaces it when selected. Above both sits a run header whose "Now" line names the active or failed step, its reason and the next CLI command before anything else. Each piece of evidence has exactly one home; every other page shows a one-line link to it. The pipeline never clips, and a node inspector is at most about two screens because long lists live in collapsed, filterable tables in the Evidence tab.

result.timeline:
**Principle:** one pure module, `src/projects/timeline.ts`, turns existing payloads into spans and rows. Two views render them: the run Timeline tab and a node-filtered Timeline tab. Durations then appear everywhere as a side effect.

**Run › Timeline tab**
1. **Phase table plus Gantt** (`run-timeline`). This is a `<table>`: one row per step in definition order, with parallel lanes as separate rows. Columns: Step | Started | Took | Tries | visual bar cell (the bar is `aria-hidden`, so the table is the accessible equivalent). Each attempt gets its own bar segment. Markers: ✗ ends a failed attempt; ⟲ marks a repair (from `node_id:null` "Repair N applied" #21); ⚡ marks a controller (re)start (PID logs #10/15/18/22/26); ‖ marks a pause; ? marks a question wait (hatched). The axis uses local HH:MM. Silences over 30 min get an axis break, so overnight outages do not squash the bars.
2. **Activity list** (`timeline-event`). Finished runs are shown oldest first and live runs newest first, with a toggle. Row format: local time (HH:MM:SS, plus relative time for the last hour), step chip (or `controller` / `operator`), status dot, and the humanized message. SHAs are cut to 7 characters, and known messages map to short text ("Awaiting explicit completion signal; idle is not acceptance" → "waiting for the worker's completion signal"). An expander shows `#sequence` and the full text. Run-level rows are inline. A diagnosis row (#19 "failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 … lane repair (RUNBOOK)") carries a **next step** tag. PID lines collapse into ⚡ chips behind a "Show controller logs" toggle (`controller-logs-toggle`). The same regex catches PID messages aliased onto `launch_controller` (guardrails #5/8/11/14/17/24/29/32).
3. **Gap rows** (`timeline-gap`) appear when events are silent for more than 2 min. The surrounding events classify them: "Waiting for the worker 28m21s" (#9→#11), "Operator 5m37s → Repair 1" (#19→#21), "Controller down 8m06s: claude not found → restarted" (guardrails #9→#11).

**Node › Timeline tab.** The same component, filtered to `node_id` plus run-level rows that name the node's lane ("worker/game", "attempts worker:game"). Rows are grouped by attempt: "Try 1 · 09:19:13–09:20:20 (1m07s) · failed: unit, integration — no passing test evidence". Expanding a try loads `results/<lane>/<k>` and shows "setup 27s · checks 40s": setup is the try's running event minus the first `checks[].started_at`. Receipts appear as timed rows here: launch requested and native started (`launch.*`), question asked, answered and waited Xm (`questions[].asked_at/answered_at`), and stop confirmed (`stop.confirmed_at`). Review nodes show one span per reviewer (`launched_at → accepted_at`, or "superseded"). Challenge attempts are parsed from the message ("Design challenge attempt N", case-insensitive), so events #1-#7 read tries 1-3 and not "attempt 1". `node-events` / `events-none` and `reuse-none` / `reuse-list` live here.

**Span derivation rules (unit-tested):**
- Node span = first status event → last terminal status event.
- Worker span = `native_started_at` (else `launch_requested_at`) → `stop.confirmed_at`, or now while running.
- Worker deadline ≈ `launch_requested_at + worker_timeout_seconds + Σ question waits`.
- Review, native transport: first review event → `reviewed_at`. Print transport: start **inferred** from the candidate's last succeeded event, end = `reviewed_at`.
- Candidate start inferred from the latest verify success.
- Approval inferred from the integrate event.
- Check duration = `finished_at − started_at`.
- Run duration = `created_at` → last activity. Last activity = the last event's `occurred_at` or `reviewed_at`, never `updated_at`, which trails activity by 3.5 min in skeleton-001 because of export rewrites (server/projects.ts:936).
- Every inferred value is prefixed ≈ and its tooltip names its source.

**Where durations show:** the header ("ran 52m51s · 08:39 → 09:32"), pipeline chips, run Summary step table, node verdict strip ("Worked 28m21s", "try 3 of 3 · 1m15s"), check rows ("unit · 2s"), reviewer rows ("general 3m49s"), and run-list rows.

**Time format:** a `<Time>` component renders `<time dateTime=iso title="2026-09-24 09:32:31 UTC">09:32</time>`. It uses local time, adds the date only when it is not today, and adds a relative suffix for headers, lists and live items. One `useNow(30s)` tick drives it; there is no per-row timer. A Local/UTC toggle for matching CLI logs is stored in localStorage (a per-viewer preference, wrapped in try/catch). `formatTime` (status.ts:100-104) becomes `formatClock`, `formatAgo` and `formatSpan`, and `formatDuration` is reused.

**Attempts:** one vocabulary. "Try n of max" for verify and candidate (`inputs.max_verification_attempts`), "Attempt n" for the challenge, "Session" for workers. The graph node attempt is shown only when it is above 1, and never for pending nodes.

result.risks:
- **Client-side rules drift from the controller.** Now-line situations, command templates, inferred spans, and question detection from message text can all fall out of step with the controller. Mitigations: keep them in one pure, unit-tested table; label inferred values with ≈ and their source; cite the RUNBOOK section; say "suggested". B3 (served attention) and a later controller `next_step` then replace the parsing.
- **Undocumented URI convention.** Earlier-attempt results depend on `results/<lane>/<k>`. A chip appears only after a 200 response, and B7 `attempt_results` makes it explicit.
- **Placeholder commands.** `"$RUN"` means commands are not paste-and-go unless B5 is enabled. Exposing a home path is a deliberate policy change, so B5 is opt-in only.
- **Clipboard on remote access.** `navigator.clipboard` needs a secure context. A Mac reaching the VPS over plain http (not an SSH tunnel to localhost) falls back to select-and-⌘C.
- **Sticky space and height.** The sticky pipeline and tab bar take about 130 px. With 3+ lanes the DAG is 3 rows tall. Mitigations: compact stuck mode, lanes merged into a "Launch ×N" group when stuck, and sticky disabled at `max-height:700px`.
- **Pipeline rebuild.** Replacing the SVG graph with HTML nodes risks regressions in keyboard handling and in test coupling. Every data attribute, the aria-label format and the edge ids are kept, and slice 3 lands behind those assertions.
- **Timezone confusion.** Local time can confuse when matching events.jsonl or CLI output (UTC). Hence the UTC toggle and the UTC `title` on every time.
- **Condensed honesty wording.** The shorter wording could lose nuance. The full sentences stay in (?) popovers, and the short visible forms keep the pinned substrings.
- **Test churn and slice order.** About 100 assertions move across 7 specs. Doing it per slice limits the blast radius, but slice 3 is large and needs a dedicated review.
- **Polling cost.** Runs home fans out N+1 requests until B2 lands; it polls at 15 s and only fetches details for non-terminal runs.
- **Large runs.** Files trees and patch parsing are client-side. Rows render lazily (collapsed groups), and diff parsing runs only when a file is expanded.
- **Honest summary of gaps.** Print-transport review times, approval times and live worker states stay inferred or missing until the controller emits B7 events. The UI must say "not recorded" rather than invent them.
